name: Bai Sau (Back Beach)
tagline: The long beach strip where most foreigners land
description: Thuy Van Street runs for several kilometres along an open sand beach, lined with condo towers like Vung Tau Melody and The Song, seafood restaurants and a wide seafront promenade. Most serviced apartments and monthly rentals sit here. It is the default base for a remote worker who wants a swim before the first call.
bestFor: Nomads who want a sea view apartment, a gym downstairs and sand two minutes from the desk.
pros: Best supply of monthly serviced apartments
Swimmable beach and a flat promenade for running
Plenty of cafes and seafood along Thuy Van
cons: Weekend crowds arrive by the busload from Ho Chi Minh City
Strong rip currents and litter after storms
Feels stretched out, you need a scooter to get around

name: Bai Truoc (Front Beach)
tagline: Old harbour downtown facing the sunset
description: The original town centre, where colonial villas, a shaded seafront park and the Xom Luoi fish market face the harbour rather than the open sea. Banks, the post office, pharmacies and the cheapest coffee in town are all within a few blocks. Walkable in a way the rest of Vung Tau is not.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to live without a scooter and be inside a real working town.
pros: Everything practical is within walking distance
Sunset views over the harbour from the park
Cheap local food and a genuine fish market
cons: The water here is not for swimming
Traffic noise on Quang Trung and Ha Long streets

name: Khu A Chau
description: A grid of quiet lanes between Phan Chu Trinh and Hoang Hoa Tham, nicknamed the Asia Area, that grew up around the offshore oil industry. Western bakeries, bars, a couple of international-style eateries and long-term house rentals cluster here. Ten minutes on foot to Front Beach, fifteen by scooter to Back Beach.
bestFor: Longer stayers who want a house, a familiar bar and neighbours who speak English.
pros: Central without the main road noise
Whole houses rentable long term, often under $400 a month
cons: Very few short-term or furnished options
Ageing expat bar scene is not for everyone

name: Bai Dau
tagline: Quiet coastal road under Big Mountain
description: A narrow shoreline strip on the north-west side of Big Mountain, known for the hillside Christ statue viewpoints, small guesthouses and a coast road with almost no traffic. Rocky coves replace sand. The calmest place to base in Vung Tau, with sunset water views from most upper-floor rooms.
bestFor: Writers and deep-focus workers who value silence over nightlife.
pros: Great sea and sunset views for the money
Scenic coast road for cycling and walks
cons: Thin on cafes, restaurants and groceries
You need a scooter for anything at all

name: Chi Linh (Ward 10)
tagline: Newer inland grid where locals actually live
description: A planned residential area north of the beaches with wide straight streets, new townhouses, local markets and a supermarket. Rents run well below the seafront towers and daily costs are local prices, not tourist ones. Roughly ten minutes by scooter to Back Beach and fifteen to Front Beach.
bestFor: Budget nomads on a long stay who are happy to ride to the beach.
pros: Cheapest decent housing in the city
Local market prices, no tourist markup
New, quiet streets with easy parking
cons: Little English spoken and few cafes to work from
Bland new-build streets with limited shade
